title: Immunization Services Course Opening Standard — Age, Consent, Repeat and Season Conditions
content:
An Immunization Services vaccination course is opened for a patient only when every condition below holds for the vaccination concerned. The figures each condition refers to (youngest and oldest age, guardian-consent age, whether another course is allowed after a completed one, days since the previous course, whether outside records are accepted, the season dates, the doses in the series, the pediatric second-dose age and whether an additional immunocompromised dose is allowed) are the vaccination's own figures in the product tables.

## Clauses

1. **Age band.** A course is opened only for a patient whose age in whole years on the planned first-dose date is at least the vaccination's youngest age and no more than its oldest age.
2. **Risk condition attestation — no longer in force.** The former clause requiring, below the vaccination's risk-condition age, that the patient attest a qualifying risk condition recorded on the course, with Kestrel recording the attestation and never asking for medical records, is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis.
3. **Guardian consent.** Below the vaccination's guardian-consent age the course is opened only with a parent or legal guardian present to sign the consent.
4. **No repeat where none is allowed.** Where the vaccination does not allow another course after a completed one, a course is not opened when the patient has a completed course of the same vaccination, whether completed at Kestrel or documented by another provider where the vaccination accepts outside records.
5. **Days since the previous course.** Where the vaccination's days-since-previous-course figure is above 0, the course is opened only when that many days have passed since the last dose of the previous course.
6. **Season.** A seasonal course is opened only between the first and the last day of its season.
7. **Doses the course requires.** The course's valid doses required are the doses in the series, plus one for a child aged no more than the pediatric second-dose age with fewer than two lifetime influenza doses, plus one for an immunocompromised patient where the vaccination allows an additional immunocompromised dose.

## Where each condition is read from

| Condition | Read from |
|---|---|
| Age on the planned first-dose date | The patient's date of birth on the Kestrel profile, against the planned first-dose date |
| Completed earlier course | The patient's vaccination courses at Kestrel, and a course documented by another provider where accepted |
| Days since the previous course | The date of the last dose of the previous course of the same vaccination |
| Immunocompromised | The patient's attestation, recorded on the course |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical patients)

- Age band, youngest age 19: a patient who turns 19 on the planned first-dose date qualifies on age; a patient who turns 19 the day after does not.
- Days since the previous course, 60 days: a planned date exactly 60 days after the last dose of the previous course qualifies; 59 days does not.
- Doses required, a single-dose vaccination with no pediatric or immunocompromised addition: 1. A child aged 7 with one lifetime influenza dose, for a vaccination whose pediatric second-dose age is 8: the doses in the series plus one.
